paragraphs.source_en: Just then, however, the sliding screen behind him was pushed open with a soft swish, and Miss Yukie respectfully served tea to the guest. Ordinarily, this shaven-headed fellow would certainly have mocked my master by saying, “Here comes savage tea,” but now, merely sitting opposite him was painful enough; and when a young lady in the flower of her age presented the teacup with a peculiarly affected gesture in the Ogasawara style she had just learned at school, the poor bald-headed fellow looked more tormented than ever, as if sitting on thorns. After Miss Yukie had served the tea, closed the sliding screen again, and withdrawn to the next room, she did nothing but giggle. Judging from this, young women of the same age are far more composed than this bald-headed gentleman; it is really quite remarkable. All the more striking was this giggle because Miss Yukie had only a little while ago shed a single red tear from vexation.

paragraphs.source_en: “If it is Class B, then I am your class supervisor.” My master said this with deep feeling; in truth, that large head had caught his eye from the day the boy entered school, so there was no question of his forgetting it. Not only that, my master had even been so impressed by the head that he sometimes saw it in dreams. Yet my careless master had been unable to connect that head with this old-fashioned name, or to connect that combination with the second-year Class B. Therefore, on hearing that the great head he had admired even in dreams belonged to a student in the class he supervised, he suddenly understood and thought, “So that is it!” But he could not imagine why this large-headed pupil, with his old-fashioned name and under his own supervision, had come at such an hour. To begin with, my master was not very popular at school, so the students there almost never came calling, whether at New Year or at year’s end. This Furui Buemon could practically be counted as the first rare visitor ever to cross his threshold. But because he could not grasp the true purpose of the visit, my master seemed greatly at a loss. He surely would not have come idly to amuse himself at the house of such a dull, stiff teacher. At the same time, if he had come to urge his teacher to resign, he would certainly have adopted a somewhat lofty bearing. Nor was it possible that he had come to consult him about some personal matter. However my master thought about it, he still could not make out the boy’s purpose. Looking at Buemon, it even seemed as though he himself did not know why he had come there. Having no other choice, my master at last asked him directly:

paragraphs.source_en: When my master said this, Buemon merely kept his head lowered and said nothing. Now this Buemon, for a second-year middle-school student, was rather eloquent; though his intelligence had not developed in proportion to his enormous head, when it came to chattering on he was one of the brightest lights in Class B. It was none other than this Buemon who, only the other day, had greatly troubled my master by asking him to explain what Columbus meant in Japanese. For this outstanding fellow to have been tongue-tied from the moment he arrived, like a stuttering young lady shut away in the inner chambers, there had to be something behind it; it could not possibly be taken as mere politeness.
